title: Customer-facing rollback and status drafts — July 2026 incident
content:
Purpose and scope:
This doc contains customer-facing drafts for the July 2026 service disruption that affected hosted inference endpoints in us-west-2. Included: three short status-page updates (initial, intermediate, resolved), a concise customer postmortem summary suitable for email/portal distribution, a plain-language root-cause explanation, timeline of events, mitigation steps we took, customer impact & recommended actions, and a small FAQ and contact/compensation note.

Guiding principles for the messaging (internal):
- Be transparent but concise; customers need facts and next steps.
- Minimize engineering jargon; focus on impact and mitigation.
- Offer clear remediation/rollback guidance where applicable.
- Include an ETA or committed follow-up when we don’t yet have a full fix.

Status page drafts (short form)
1) Initial (posted at 2026-07-24T08:12Z) — SHORT:
Title: Degraded hosted inference performance in us-west-2
Message: We are investigating reports of elevated latency and intermittent errors for hosted inference endpoints in the US West (us-west-2) region. Some requests may time out or return 5xx errors. Our SRE and runtime teams are actively investigating. We will provide an update within 30 minutes.
Impact: Some hosted API requests (text generation, embeddings) in us-west-2 may experience slow or failed responses.
2) Update (posted at 2026-07-24T09:05Z) — INTERMEDIATE:
Title: Partial mitigation deployed; rollback in progress for specific model variants
Message: We have identified a regression introduced during a kernel/optimization rollout that increased memory pressure for certain model families under sustained traffic patterns. We have deployed a partial mitigation (traffic throttling + autoscaling override) for affected pools and started a controlled rollback to the previous runtime variant. Customers using pinned model versions are unaffected. We expect reduced errors for most customers in the next 30–60 minutes. If you continue to see errors after 10:00Z, please contact support with request IDs.
Impact: Reduced error rates for affected endpoints; some customers may still see brief failures while rollback completes.
3) Resolved (posted at 2026-07-24T10:30Z) — FINAL:
Title: Incident resolved — hosted inference performance restored in us-west-2
Message: The rollback completed and monitoring indicates stable latency and error rates within normal bounds. Root cause analysis is underway and a customer-facing postmortem will be published within 3 business days. If you observe residual issues, please open a support ticket and include example request IDs and timestamps.
Impact: Services are restored; pinning to model versions remained safe during the incident.

Customer-facing postmortem summary (concise, ~3–5 paragraphs)
We sincerely apologize for the disruption to hosted inference endpoints in US West (us-west-2) on July 24, 2026. Between approximately 08:10Z and 10:25Z, a subset of hosted API requests experienced elevated latency and intermittent 5xx errors. The incident affected a portion of customers whose traffic hit specific runtime pools serving recent kernel optimizations.
What happened (plain language): On July 24 we rolled an updated runtime optimization intended to improve throughput for a set of model architectures. Under certain real-world traffic patterns the new kernels increased system memory pressure and led to degraded request handling for some GPU pools. As a result, some requests were dropped or retried, producing timeouts and 5xx responses.
What we did: Our detection systems alerted SRE and runtime on-call; we scoped the impact to specific pools and immediately throttled traffic to those pools while enabling autoscaling overrides. We then executed a controlled rollback to the prior runtime kernel for affected pools; the rollback finished at 10:25Z and monitoring shows error and latency graphs returned to baseline.
Customer impact: Affected customers saw higher latencies and sporadic failed requests during the window. Customers who had pinned to model versions or used Dedicated/Private deployments were not materially affected. We recognize this caused user-facing issues for downstream applications and are sorry for the disruption.
Next steps and mitigation to prevent recurrence: We are pausing automatic kernel rollouts until we complete expanded integration tests that include representative traffic profiles and memory-pressure scenarios. We will add an automated smoke test that validates memory behavior under sustained concurrency before any future rollout. We will also refine canary criteria so smaller traffic buckets are validated longer before broad rollout.
Compensation and support: If you experienced business impact, our customer-success team will reach out proactively with credits or account remediation options. If you need immediate assistance, open a ticket referencing INC-7894 and include example request IDs.

Technical root cause (concise for customers comfortable with a bit more detail)
- Trigger: an optimization change to kernel scheduling and memory allocation for attention and KV-cache paths was deployed to runtime pools serving several popular open models.
- Failure mode: under sustained, varied prompt lengths and high-concurrency traffic, the change caused fragmentation and transient spikes in device memory usage. The spikes led to OOM safety mechanisms preemptively rejecting inflight requests and causing retries/timeouts.
- Why it bypassed our safeguards: our canary tests exercised throughput and latency but did not sufficiently replicate the long-tail concurrency + prompt-length distribution seen in production for these model families.

Incident timeline (high level)
- 08:10Z — First alerts: elevated 5xx and latency from us-west-2 runtime pools.
- 08:12Z — Status page initial post and on-call pages notified.
- 08:20Z — SRE and runtime engineers triaged; confirmed correlation with kernel rollout.
- 08:40Z — Traffic throttles and autoscaling overrides applied to affected pools.
- 09:05Z — Controlled rollback initiated for targeted runtime variant.
- 10:25Z — Rollback completed; monitoring returned to normal.
- 10:30Z — Resolved status posted to the status page.

Customer recommended actions
- If you rely on pinned model versions for stability, continue current pinning; no change needed.
- For customers using hosted endpoints without pins, consider temporarily pinning to a known good model version if you need stricter predictability while we validate rollout changes.
- Provide examples: when filing a ticket, include sample request IDs, timestamps (UTC), the model id, and a brief description of client-side behavior (timeouts, errors).

FAQ (short)
Q: Were my data or prompts exposed?
A: No. This was a runtime performance regression that led to failed requests; there is no evidence of data leakage.
Q: Is Dedicated/Private affected?
A: Dedicated capacity and Private deployments were not materially affected unless customers opted into the new runtime variant during a private upgrade window.
Q: Will you change release cadence?
A: We will not broadly change cadence but will strengthen pre-rollout requirements (longer canaries, additional memory-stress tests, better traffic simulation).

Customer email template (short version)
Subject: Incident resolved — hosted inference in us-west-2 (Jul 24)
Hi <CustomerName>,
We wanted to let you know we resolved an incident that affected hosted inference in US West on Jul 24. The issue was caused by a runtime optimization that increased memory pressure for certain model pools; we rolled back the change and performance has been restored. We sincerely apologize for any disruption. If you saw errors, please reply with example request IDs and we’ll prioritize investigation and remediation.
Best — Marina Chen (on behalf of Redwood Inference SRE & Customer Success)

Internal notes (for CS + SRE handoff)
- Prioritize outreach to customers with SLAs and any who filed tickets during 08:10–10:30Z.
- Prepare tailored credits for customers with measurable business impact; coordinate with finance on thresholds.
- Engineering to produce a detailed RCA doc in Confluence and schedule a 60-minute review with product and release teams.
- Revisit canary policy and update rollout playbook by Aug 7.

Draft Slack/Teams snippet for CS channels
"Incident update: us-west-2 runtime regression caused transient 5xxs between 08:10–10:25Z. Rollback completed, services restored. CS to triage impacted accounts and offer remediation; see INC-7894 for details."

End of draft doc.
Notes to self: get sign-off from runtime lead (Evan) and head of SRE (Diego) before publishing to status.redwood.ai and sending outbound customer email.
